title: Boxers and Qing troops besiege the foreign legations in Beijing
summary: Boxer fighters and Qing imperial troops began a siege of the Legation Quarter in Beijing, trapping foreign diplomats, soldiers and Chinese Christians for 55 days until an international relief force arrived.
reason: Anger at foreign domination, missionaries and economic upheaval fed the anti-foreign Boxer movement, which the Qing court decided to back after the killing of the German minister.
significance: The siege provoked the Eight-Nation Alliance intervention and left China saddled with a crushing indemnity that weakened the Qing dynasty further.

title: Max Planck presents the quantum hypothesis
summary: Max Planck presented his derivation of the law of black-body radiation to the German Physical Society in Berlin, assuming that energy is emitted in discrete packets, or quanta.
reason: Classical physics could not explain the measured spectrum of radiation from hot bodies, and Planck sought a formula that fit the experimental data.
significance: The talk is regarded as the birth of quantum theory, which reshaped physics and modern technology.

title: The six Australian colonies federate as the Commonwealth of Australia
summary: The Commonwealth of Australia was proclaimed at a ceremony in Centennial Park, Sydney, uniting six British colonies into one federal dominion with Edmund Barton as first prime minister.
reason: Concerns over defence, trade barriers between colonies and a growing sense of shared national identity drove the federation movement through the 1890s.
significance: It created the Australian nation and its federal constitution, still in force today.

title: China signs the Boxer Protocol
summary: The Qing government signed the Boxer Protocol with eleven foreign powers in Beijing, agreeing to pay a huge indemnity, execute officials and allow foreign troops to be stationed in the capital.
reason: The foreign powers that had crushed the Boxer Rebellion imposed punishment and guarantees after occupying Beijing.
significance: It deepened China's humiliation and financial ruin, discrediting the Qing dynasty in the decade before its fall.

title: The first Nobel Prizes are awarded
summary: The first Nobel Prizes in physics, chemistry, medicine and literature were presented in Stockholm on the anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death, with the peace prize awarded in Christiania.
reason: Alfred Nobel left most of his fortune in his will to fund annual prizes for those who conferred the greatest benefit on humankind.
significance: The Nobel Prizes became the most prestigious awards in science, literature and peace.

title: Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal
summary: Guglielmo Marconi reported receiving the Morse letter S, sent from Poldhu in Cornwall, at Signal Hill in St. John's, Newfoundland, using a kite-borne antenna.
reason: Marconi wanted to prove that wireless signals could travel beyond the horizon and compete with undersea telegraph cables.
significance: It showed long-distance radio was possible and launched the era of global wireless communication.

title: Mount Pelee erupts and destroys Saint-Pierre
summary: A pyroclastic flow from Mount Pelee on Martinique swept over the town of Saint-Pierre, killing about 28,000 people within minutes; only a handful survived.
reason: The volcano had shown warning signs for weeks, but authorities kept residents in town, partly because of an upcoming election.
significance: It was the deadliest volcanic eruption of the twentieth century and transformed the study of volcanic hazards.

title: Treaty of Vereeniging ends the Second Boer War
summary: Boer leaders and British representatives signed the Treaty of Vereeniging in Pretoria, ending the Second Boer War and bringing the Transvaal and Orange Free State under British rule.
reason: After years of guerrilla war, scorched-earth tactics and deaths in concentration camps, the Boer commandos could no longer continue fighting.
significance: It ended Boer independence and set the stage for the Union of South Africa in 1910.

title: Panama declares independence from Colombia
summary: Panamanian separatists declared independence from Colombia in Panama City, protected by United States warships that blocked Colombian troops from landing.
reason: Colombia's Senate had rejected a treaty letting the United States build a canal, so Washington backed Panamanian separatists to secure the route.
significance: It created the Republic of Panama and opened the way for the American-built Panama Canal.

title: The Wright brothers make the first powered airplane flight
summary: Orville Wright flew the Wright Flyer for 12 seconds near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, the first sustained, controlled flight of a powered heavier-than-air aircraft; four flights were made that day.
reason: Wilbur and Orville Wright had spent years studying flight control, building gliders and a wind tunnel, and designing a light engine and propellers.
significance: It began the age of aviation, which transformed travel, trade and war.
place: Kill Devil Hills, North Carolina, United States

title: Japan attacks Port Arthur, starting the Russo-Japanese War
summary: The Japanese navy launched a surprise torpedo attack on the Russian Pacific Squadron at Port Arthur in Manchuria, opening the Russo-Japanese War.
reason: Japan and Russia competed for control of Korea and Manchuria, and negotiations had broken down.
significance: The war that followed ended with the first modern victory of an Asian power over a European one.

title: Britain and France sign the Entente Cordiale
summary: Britain and France signed a series of agreements in London settling colonial disputes, notably recognizing British control of Egypt and French influence in Morocco.
reason: Both countries wanted to end old colonial rivalries and were increasingly wary of German power.
significance: It ended centuries of Anglo-French hostility and laid the basis of the alliance that fought together in World War I.

title: German troops defeat the Herero at the Battle of Waterberg
summary: German colonial forces under Lothar von Trotha attacked the Herero at the Waterberg plateau and drove survivors into the Omaheke desert, where many died of thirst.
reason: The Herero had risen against German land seizures and abuses in German South West Africa, and von Trotha sought their destruction.
significance: It began the Herero and Nama genocide, often called the first genocide of the twentieth century.

title: Bloody Sunday: troops fire on marchers in St. Petersburg
summary: Imperial troops fired on a peaceful procession of workers led by the priest Georgy Gapon who were marching to the Winter Palace to petition the Tsar, killing and wounding hundreds.
reason: Workers were suffering harsh conditions and defeat in the war with Japan had increased discontent with autocratic rule.
significance: The massacre sparked the Russian Revolution of 1905 and destroyed popular faith in the Tsar.

title: Japan destroys the Russian fleet at Tsushima
summary: Admiral Togo Heihachiro's fleet annihilated the Russian Baltic Fleet in the Tsushima Strait after its months-long voyage around the world.
reason: Russia had sent its Baltic Fleet to break Japanese control of the seas after the fall of Port Arthur.
significance: The decisive battle forced Russia to seek peace and established Japan as a major naval power.
place: Tsushima Strait, between Korea and Japan

title: Einstein submits his paper on special relativity
summary: Albert Einstein, a clerk at the Swiss patent office in Bern, submitted On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies to Annalen der Physik, setting out the theory of special relativity.
reason: Einstein sought to reconcile Maxwell's electromagnetism with the principle that the laws of physics are the same for all observers in uniform motion.
significance: Special relativity overturned absolute space and time and became a pillar of modern physics.

title: Treaty of Portsmouth ends the Russo-Japanese War
summary: Russia and Japan signed a peace treaty at the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard in the United States, mediated by President Theodore Roosevelt; Japan gained Port Arthur, southern Sakhalin and control over Korea.
reason: Both sides were exhausted: Russia faced revolution at home and Japan was near the limit of its finances.
significance: It confirmed Japan as a great power and earned Roosevelt the Nobel Peace Prize.
place: Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, Kittery, United States

title: The partition of Bengal takes effect
summary: The British administration under Lord Curzon divided the province of Bengal into a Muslim-majority east and a Hindu-majority west, triggering mass protests and boycotts of British goods.
reason: The British cited administrative efficiency, but nationalists saw it as a way to divide and weaken Bengali political opposition.
significance: It launched the Swadeshi movement and became a turning point for Indian nationalism.

title: Earthquake and fire devastate San Francisco
summary: A major earthquake on the San Andreas Fault struck northern California, and the fires that followed destroyed most of San Francisco, killing around 3,000 people.
reason: Stress built up along the San Andreas Fault was released in a sudden rupture hundreds of kilometers long.
significance: It was one of the worst disasters in American history and advanced the science of earthquakes.

title: The Shah of Persia agrees to a constitution
summary: Mozaffar ad-Din Shah Qajar signed a decree agreeing to create an elected parliament, the Majlis, a victory for the Persian Constitutional Revolution.
reason: Merchants, clergy and reformers protested against royal corruption, foreign concessions and arbitrary rule, staging mass sit-ins in Tehran.
significance: It made Persia one of the first countries in Asia with a constitution and parliament.

title: Gandhi launches satyagraha in Johannesburg
summary: At a mass meeting of Indians in the Empire Theatre in Johannesburg, Mohandas Gandhi led a pledge to resist a discriminatory registration law through nonviolent disobedience.
reason: The Transvaal government had proposed an ordinance forcing all Indians to register and carry passes.
significance: It began the method of nonviolent resistance Gandhi later used in India and that inspired civil rights movements worldwide.

title: Oil is struck at Masjed Soleyman in Persia
summary: A drilling team financed by William Knox D'Arcy struck oil at Masjed Soleyman in southwestern Persia, the first commercial oil discovery in the Middle East.
reason: D'Arcy held a concession from the Shah and had spent years searching for oil before his funds nearly ran out.
significance: It led to the Anglo-Persian Oil Company and made the Middle East central to the world's energy and politics.

title: The Tunguska explosion flattens a Siberian forest
summary: A huge explosion over the Podkamennaya Tunguska River in Siberia flattened about 80 million trees across more than 2,000 square kilometers.
reason: It is thought to have been caused by a meteoroid or comet fragment bursting in the air several kilometers above the ground.
significance: It is the largest impact event in recorded history and a key case in assessing asteroid risks.

title: Young Turk Revolution restores the Ottoman constitution
summary: Faced with a mutiny of army officers in Macedonia, Sultan Abdul Hamid II restored the 1876 constitution and recalled parliament, beginning the Second Constitutional Era.
reason: The Committee of Union and Progress and reformist officers wanted to end autocracy and save the empire from collapse and foreign intervention.
significance: It brought the Young Turks to power and reshaped the late Ottoman Empire.

title: Ford introduces the Model T
summary: The Ford Motor Company released the Model T, a simple, durable and affordable automobile built in Detroit.
reason: Henry Ford aimed to build a car that ordinary working families could afford.
significance: The Model T put the world on wheels and helped create the mass consumer economy.

title: Louis Bleriot flies across the English Channel
summary: French aviator Louis Bleriot flew his Bleriot XI monoplane from near Calais to Dover in about 37 minutes, the first flight across a large body of water in a heavier-than-air aircraft.
reason: The Daily Mail newspaper offered a prize for the first flight across the Channel.
significance: It showed that Britain was no longer protected by the sea and boosted public faith in aviation.

title: The Union of South Africa is formed
summary: The Cape, Natal, Transvaal and Orange River colonies were united into the Union of South Africa, a self-governing British dominion with Louis Botha as prime minister.
reason: After the Boer War, British and Boer leaders sought a unified state, built on a settlement that excluded most black Africans from political power.
significance: It founded the modern South African state and entrenched the racial order that led to apartheid.

title: Japan annexes Korea
summary: Representatives of Japan and the Korean Empire signed the annexation treaty in Seoul, making Korea a Japanese colony; it was made public a week later.
reason: Japan had made Korea a protectorate after defeating Russia and moved to full control to secure its strategic and economic interests.
significance: It began 35 years of Japanese colonial rule over Korea.

title: Madero calls for revolt, starting the Mexican Revolution
summary: Francisco Madero's Plan of San Luis Potosi called for Mexicans to rise up against President Porfirio Diaz on 20 November, the date now marked as the start of the Mexican Revolution.
reason: Diaz had ruled for over three decades, rigged the 1910 election and presided over vast inequality in land ownership.
significance: It began a decade of revolution that reshaped Mexico's politics, land and society.

title: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire kills 146 workers
summary: A fire in a garment factory in Manhattan killed 146 workers, mostly young immigrant women, many of whom were trapped by locked doors or jumped to their deaths.
reason: Exits were locked to prevent theft and breaks, and the building lacked adequate fire escapes and sprinklers.
significance: It led to major workplace safety laws and strengthened the American labor movement.
place: Asch Building, New York City, United States

title: Hiram Bingham reaches Machu Picchu
summary: Guided by local farmers, American explorer Hiram Bingham reached the ruins of the Inca citadel of Machu Picchu high in the Peruvian Andes.
reason: Bingham was searching for Vilcabamba, the last refuge of the Inca, and relied on local knowledge of ruins in the area.
significance: It brought Machu Picchu to world attention, and it became a symbol of Inca civilization.

title: The Wuchang Uprising begins the Xinhai Revolution
summary: Revolutionary soldiers of the New Army mutinied in Wuchang and seized the city, setting off a chain of provincial uprisings against the Qing dynasty.
reason: Anti-Manchu and republican groups had spread within the army, and the accidental discovery of their plans forced them to act early.
significance: It led to the fall of the Qing dynasty and the end of over two thousand years of imperial rule in China.

title: Roald Amundsen reaches the South Pole
summary: A Norwegian party of five led by Roald Amundsen reached the South Pole using dog sledges, five weeks ahead of Robert Falcon Scott's British expedition.
reason: Amundsen changed his plans from the North Pole after hearing it had been claimed, and raced Scott to the south.
significance: It was the first human arrival at the South Pole, a peak of the heroic age of polar exploration.

title: Sun Yat-sen proclaims the Republic of China
summary: Sun Yat-sen was inaugurated in Nanjing as provisional president of the newly proclaimed Republic of China.
reason: Revolutionary provinces that had broken away from the Qing needed a common government after the Wuchang Uprising.
significance: It established the first republic in Asia.
wikipedia: Provisional Government of the Republic of China (1912)

title: The African National Congress is founded
summary: African leaders met in Bloemfontein and founded the South African Native National Congress, later renamed the African National Congress.
reason: Black South Africans were excluded from power in the new Union and needed a united voice to defend their land and rights.
significance: The ANC led the struggle against apartheid and has governed South Africa since 1994.

title: The last Qing emperor abdicates
summary: Empress Dowager Longyu issued an edict on behalf of the six-year-old Puyi, abdicating the throne and transferring power to the Republic of China.
reason: After the revolution, Yuan Shikai negotiated the abdication in exchange for becoming president of the republic.
significance: It ended the Qing dynasty and over two millennia of imperial rule in China.
wikipedia: Imperial Edict of the Abdication of the Qing Emperor

title: RMS Titanic sinks in the North Atlantic
summary: The British liner Titanic, on its maiden voyage, sank in the early hours after striking an iceberg, and more than 1,500 people died.
reason: The ship was steaming fast through an ice field and carried lifeboats for only about half of those aboard.
significance: The disaster led to major reforms in maritime safety, including the first SOLAS convention.
place: North Atlantic Ocean, south of Newfoundland

title: The Rite of Spring premieres in Paris
summary: The Ballets Russes premiered Igor Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring with choreography by Vaslav Nijinsky at the Theatre des Champs-Elysees, provoking an uproar in the audience.
reason: Stravinsky and Nijinsky broke with tradition through harsh dissonance, irregular rhythms and primitive-looking dance.
significance: It became a landmark of modernism in music and dance.

title: Ford starts the moving assembly line
summary: Ford's Highland Park plant began producing complete Model T cars on a moving assembly line, cutting the time to build a car from about 12 hours to about 90 minutes.
reason: Ford wanted to meet enormous demand and lower costs by dividing work into simple repeated tasks.
significance: Mass production on the assembly line transformed industry around the world.

title: Archduke Franz Ferdinand is assassinated in Sarajevo
summary: Gavrilo Princip, a Bosnian Serb nationalist, shot dead the heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne Franz Ferdinand and his wife Sophie in Sarajevo.
reason: Young Bosnia and the Black Hand sought to end Austro-Hungarian rule over South Slavs.
significance: The killing triggered the July Crisis that led to World War I.
place: Latin Bridge, Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina

title: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia
summary: Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia by telegram, and alliance commitments drew Russia, Germany, France and Britain into war within a week.
reason: Vienna blamed Serbia for the Sarajevo assassination and, backed by Germany, issued an ultimatum it expected Serbia to reject.
significance: It began World War I, which killed millions and remade the world order.

title: The Panama Canal opens to shipping
summary: The cargo ship SS Ancon made the first official transit of the Panama Canal, linking the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
reason: The United States built the canal over a decade to shorten sea routes and strengthen its naval and commercial reach.
significance: It transformed world shipping and became one of the most important trade routes on Earth.

title: First Battle of the Marne begins
summary: French and British armies counterattacked German forces east of Paris along the Marne, forcing them to retreat to the Aisne.
reason: The German Schlieffen Plan aimed to defeat France quickly, but its armies had become overstretched and opened gaps.
significance: It ended German hopes of a swift victory and led to years of trench warfare on the Western Front.

title: Gandhi returns to India from South Africa
summary: Mohandas Gandhi landed at Bombay after more than two decades in South Africa, where he had developed his method of nonviolent resistance.
reason: Gandhi had won concessions in South Africa and was urged by Gopal Krishna Gokhale to join the Indian national movement.
significance: Gandhi went on to lead India's independence struggle; the day is marked as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.

title: Japan presents the Twenty-One Demands to China
summary: Japan secretly presented the government of Yuan Shikai with a list of demands that would have greatly extended Japanese control over Chinese territory and economy.
reason: With the European powers absorbed in World War I, Japan sought to secure its position in Shandong and Manchuria.
significance: It fueled Chinese nationalism and anti-Japanese sentiment for decades.

title: Germany releases poison gas at Ypres
summary: German troops released chlorine gas against French and colonial troops near Ypres, opening the Second Battle of Ypres with the first large-scale use of poison gas on the Western Front.
reason: Germany sought a way to break the stalemate of trench warfare.
significance: It introduced chemical warfare on a mass scale, later banned by the Geneva Protocol.

title: Ottoman arrest of Armenian leaders begins the Armenian genocide
summary: Ottoman authorities arrested hundreds of Armenian intellectuals and community leaders in Constantinople, most of whom were later killed.
reason: The Young Turk government, at war and suspicious of Armenians as a disloyal minority, set out to destroy the Armenian population of Anatolia.
significance: The date marks the start of the Armenian genocide, in which around a million people died.
wikipedia: Deportation of Armenian intellectuals on 24 April 1915

title: Allied troops land at Gallipoli
summary: Australian and New Zealand troops landed at what became Anzac Cove on the Gallipoli peninsula, as British and French forces landed elsewhere, beginning a failed eight-month campaign.
reason: The Allies hoped to knock the Ottoman Empire out of the war and open a sea route to Russia through the Dardanelles.
significance: The campaign shaped national identity in Australia, New Zealand and Turkey, and made Mustafa Kemal famous.
participants: Australian and New Zealand Army Corps

title: A German U-boat sinks the Lusitania
summary: The German submarine U-20 torpedoed the British liner Lusitania off the south coast of Ireland, killing nearly 1,200 people, including 128 Americans.
reason: Germany had declared the waters around Britain a war zone and was waging submarine warfare against Allied shipping.
significance: It turned American opinion against Germany and contributed to US entry into the war.
place: Off the Old Head of Kinsale, Ireland

title: Einstein presents the field equations of general relativity
summary: Albert Einstein presented the final field equations of general relativity to the Prussian Academy of Sciences in Berlin, describing gravity as the curvature of spacetime.
reason: Einstein had worked for years to extend relativity to gravity and acceleration.
significance: General relativity became the foundation of cosmology and of technologies such as GPS.

title: The Battle of Verdun begins
summary: German forces opened a massive bombardment and offensive against French positions around Verdun, starting a ten-month battle that cost about 700,000 casualties.
reason: German commander Erich von Falkenhayn aimed to bleed the French army white at a place it would not abandon.
significance: It became the longest battle of World War I and a lasting symbol of French resolve and of the war's futility.

title: The Easter Rising begins in Dublin
summary: Irish republicans seized the General Post Office and other sites in Dublin and proclaimed an Irish Republic; the rising was crushed within a week.
reason: Republicans wanted independence from Britain and saw the world war as an opportunity.
significance: The executions of its leaders turned Irish opinion toward independence.

title: Britain and France conclude the Sykes-Picot Agreement
summary: British and French diplomats secretly agreed on how to divide the Arab lands of the Ottoman Empire into zones of control and influence after the war.
reason: The two powers wanted to secure their postwar interests in the Middle East while fighting the Ottomans.
significance: It shaped the borders of the modern Middle East and remains a symbol of Western betrayal in the Arab world.

title: Sharif Hussein launches the Arab Revolt
summary: Sharif Hussein bin Ali of Mecca proclaimed a revolt against Ottoman rule, and his forces attacked the Ottoman garrison in Mecca.
reason: Hussein sought an independent Arab state and had British promises of support in the Hussein-McMahon correspondence.
significance: The revolt helped end Ottoman rule in the Arab lands and launched modern Arab nationalism.

title: The Battle of the Somme begins
summary: British and French troops attacked German lines along the Somme; the British army suffered about 57,000 casualties on the first day alone.
reason: The Allies planned a joint offensive to break through, which also became a way to relieve pressure on the French at Verdun.
significance: It became one of the bloodiest battles in history and a symbol of the slaughter of World War I.

title: Mexico promulgates its revolutionary constitution
summary: A constitutional congress in Queretaro adopted a new constitution for Mexico with land reform, labor rights and limits on the Church and foreign ownership of resources.
reason: The victorious revolutionary faction of Venustiano Carranza needed to consolidate power and address the demands of peasants and workers.
significance: It was among the first constitutions to guarantee social rights and is still in force today.

title: The February Revolution begins in Petrograd
summary: Protests and strikes over bread shortages broke out in Petrograd and grew into a revolt joined by soldiers, forcing Tsar Nicholas II to abdicate within a week.
reason: War losses, food shortages and contempt for the Tsar's government had made the regime deeply unpopular.
significance: It ended three centuries of Romanov rule and opened the path to the Bolshevik seizure of power.

title: The United States declares war on Germany
summary: The US Congress voted to declare war on Germany at President Woodrow Wilson's request, bringing the United States into World War I.
reason: Germany had resumed unrestricted submarine warfare and the Zimmermann Telegram revealed a plot to ally with Mexico.
significance: American troops and resources tipped the balance toward the Allies and made the US a world power.
place: United States Capitol, Washington, D.C., United States
wikipedia: American entry into World War I

title: Three children report a vision of Mary at Fatima
summary: Three shepherd children in Fatima, Portugal, reported seeing the Virgin Mary at the Cova da Iria, the first of a series of reported apparitions.
reason: The visions came in a deeply Catholic rural region during the turmoil of World War I and Portugal's anticlerical republic.
significance: Fatima became one of the most visited Catholic pilgrimage sites in the world.

title: Britain issues the Balfour Declaration
summary: British Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour sent a letter to Lord Rothschild stating government support for a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine.
reason: Britain sought Jewish support for the war effort and a strategic foothold in Palestine near the Suez Canal.
significance: It laid the political groundwork for the State of Israel and the Arab-Israeli conflict.

title: The Bolsheviks seize power in the October Revolution
summary: Bolshevik-led Red Guards took key points in Petrograd and stormed the Winter Palace, overthrowing the Provisional Government and handing power to the Soviets.
reason: The Provisional Government had kept Russia in the war and failed to deliver land and bread, while Lenin's Bolsheviks won over workers and soldiers.
significance: It created the first communist state and shaped world politics for most of the century.

title: Finland declares independence from Russia
summary: The Finnish parliament approved a declaration of independence, ending more than a century as a grand duchy of the Russian Empire.
reason: The Russian revolutions had left a power vacuum, and Finnish leaders feared Bolshevik rule.
significance: It founded the independent Finnish state; 6 December is its national day.

title: Soviet Russia signs the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
summary: Soviet Russia signed a separate peace with the Central Powers at Brest-Litovsk, giving up Poland, the Baltic lands, Finland and Ukraine.
reason: Lenin needed to end the war to save the Bolshevik regime after the Russian army collapsed.
significance: It took Russia out of World War I and let Germany shift troops to the Western Front.

title: The Bolsheviks kill the Romanov family
summary: Former Tsar Nicholas II, his wife, their five children and four servants were shot by Bolshevik guards in the Ipatiev House in Yekaterinburg.
reason: With White forces approaching the city, the Bolsheviks feared the family could be rescued and become a rallying point.
significance: It ended the Romanov dynasty and signaled the ruthlessness of the Civil War.

title: Germany is proclaimed a republic as the Kaiser falls
summary: As revolution spread, Chancellor Max von Baden announced Kaiser Wilhelm II's abdication and Philipp Scheidemann proclaimed a republic from the Reichstag balcony.
reason: Military defeat, naval mutinies and mass strikes had destroyed support for the monarchy.
significance: It ended the German Empire and began the Weimar Republic.

title: Armistice ends the fighting of World War I
summary: Germany signed an armistice with the Allies in a railway carriage in the forest of Compiegne, and fighting on the Western Front stopped at 11 a.m.
reason: Germany's army was retreating, its allies had collapsed, and revolution had broken out at home.
significance: It ended World War I, in which about 20 million people died.
place: Glade of the Armistice, Compiegne, France

title: Koreans declare independence in the March 1st Movement
summary: Korean leaders read a declaration of independence in Seoul, sparking peaceful demonstrations across Korea that Japanese authorities suppressed violently.
reason: Koreans resented harsh Japanese colonial rule and were inspired by Wilson's call for self-determination.
significance: It led to the Provisional Government of Korea and remains central to Korean national identity.

title: British troops massacre civilians at Jallianwala Bagh
summary: Troops under General Reginald Dyer fired without warning on a crowd gathered in the Jallianwala Bagh garden in Amritsar, killing hundreds of unarmed people.
reason: British authorities feared unrest after protests against the Rowlatt Act and had banned public gatherings.
significance: The massacre turned many Indians against British rule and strengthened the independence movement.

title: Students protest in Beijing in the May Fourth Movement
summary: Thousands of students gathered at Tiananmen in Beijing to protest the decision at Versailles to hand German rights in Shandong to Japan.
reason: Chinese anger at the weak government and foreign humiliation combined with a wider movement for cultural renewal.
significance: It shaped modern Chinese nationalism and fed the rise of the Chinese Communist Party.

title: Eclipse observations confirm Einstein's bending of light
summary: Expeditions led by Arthur Eddington on the island of Principe and by others in Sobral, Brazil, photographed stars during a total solar eclipse to measure the bending of starlight by the Sun.
reason: General relativity predicted a deflection twice that of Newtonian physics, and an eclipse was the only way to test it.
significance: The results confirmed general relativity and made Einstein world famous.
place: Roca Sundy, Principe, Sao Tome and Principe

title: The Treaty of Versailles is signed
summary: Germany and the Allied powers signed the peace treaty in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, imposing territorial losses, disarmament and reparations on Germany.
reason: The victors wanted to punish Germany, secure France and build a new order including the League of Nations.
significance: It formally ended World War I and its terms fueled resentment that helped bring about World War II.
place: Hall of Mirrors, Palace of Versailles, France

title: The League of Nations comes into being
summary: The Covenant of the League of Nations took effect with the Treaty of Versailles, creating the first worldwide organization to keep the peace.
reason: After the catastrophe of World War I, statesmen led by Woodrow Wilson sought collective security to prevent new wars.
significance: Though it failed to stop World War II, it was the forerunner of the United Nations.

title: The Grand National Assembly of Turkey opens in Ankara
summary: Turkish nationalists led by Mustafa Kemal opened a new parliament in Ankara that rejected the authority of the Allied-occupied Ottoman government.
reason: The Allies had occupied Constantinople and planned to partition Anatolia, so nationalists formed a rival government.
significance: It led the War of Independence and became the parliament of the Republic of Turkey.

title: Tennessee ratifies women's suffrage in the United States
summary: Tennessee became the 36th state to ratify the Nineteenth Amendment, giving it the support needed to guarantee American women the right to vote.
reason: Decades of campaigning by suffragists and women's wartime contribution built support for the amendment.
significance: It enfranchised millions of women and was a milestone for women's rights worldwide.
place: Tennessee State Capitol, Nashville, United States
wikipedia: Nineteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution

title: KDKA makes the first commercial radio broadcast
summary: Pittsburgh station KDKA broadcast the results of the Harding-Cox presidential election, widely regarded as the start of commercial radio broadcasting.
reason: Westinghouse launched the station to create demand for the radio receivers it manufactured.
significance: It launched the era of mass broadcasting that transformed news, politics and entertainment.

title: Reza Khan seizes Tehran in a coup
summary: Cossack Brigade officer Reza Khan and journalist Zia'eddin Tabatabaee marched into Tehran with troops and took control of the government.
reason: Persia was weak, divided and under foreign influence, and reformers and British officials wanted a stronger central government.
significance: It brought Reza Khan to power; he became Reza Shah and founded the Pahlavi dynasty.

title: The Chinese Communist Party holds its first congress
summary: A small group of delegates, including Mao Zedong, met secretly in Shanghai's French Concession for the first national congress of the Chinese Communist Party.
reason: Inspired by the Russian Revolution and supported by the Comintern, Chinese radicals sought to organize a Marxist party.
significance: The party it founded went on to rule China from 1949.
wikipedia: 1st National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party

title: Insulin is first given to a diabetic patient
summary: At Toronto General Hospital, 14-year-old Leonard Thompson received the first injection of insulin extract to treat type 1 diabetes.
reason: Frederick Banting and Charles Best had isolated insulin from dog pancreases the year before, and doctors sought a treatment for a disease that was then fatal.
significance: Insulin turned diabetes from a death sentence into a treatable condition for millions.

title: Britain declares Egypt independent
summary: Britain unilaterally ended its protectorate over Egypt and recognized it as an independent kingdom, while keeping control of defense, the Suez Canal and Sudan.
reason: The Egyptian Revolution of 1919 and continued nationalist pressure made the protectorate untenable.
significance: It made Egypt formally independent under King Fuad I, though British influence remained strong.

title: Mussolini's Fascists march on Rome
summary: Thousands of Fascist Blackshirts converged on Rome, and King Victor Emmanuel III refused to declare martial law and soon asked Benito Mussolini to form a government.
reason: Postwar unrest, fear of socialism and a weak liberal state let the Fascists present themselves as a force for order.
significance: It brought the first fascist government to power in Europe.

title: The Turkish parliament abolishes the Ottoman sultanate
summary: The Grand National Assembly in Ankara voted to abolish the Ottoman sultanate, and the last sultan, Mehmed VI, left Constantinople weeks later.
reason: Victory in the War of Independence gave Mustafa Kemal's nationalists the authority to end the dual government.
significance: It ended the Ottoman Empire after more than six centuries.

title: Howard Carter finds the tomb of Tutankhamun
summary: Howard Carter's team uncovered the first step leading down to the almost intact tomb of the pharaoh Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings.
reason: Carter, funded by Lord Carnarvon, had searched the valley for years for a tomb he believed was still undiscovered.
significance: It became the most famous archaeological find in history and sparked worldwide interest in ancient Egypt.
place: Valley of the Kings, Luxor, Egypt

title: The Soviet Union is founded
summary: Delegates from Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and the Transcaucasian republic approved the treaty creating the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics in Moscow.
reason: After winning the Civil War, the Bolsheviks needed a formal structure to bind the Soviet republics under one government.
significance: The USSR became a superpower that shaped the twentieth century until its collapse in 1991.
wikipedia: Treaty on the Creation of the USSR

title: The Treaty of Lausanne recognizes modern Turkey
summary: Turkey and the Allied powers signed a peace treaty in Lausanne that replaced the Treaty of Sevres and recognized the borders of a sovereign Turkish state.
reason: Turkish victory in the War of Independence forced the Allies to negotiate new terms.
significance: It set Turkey's modern borders and confirmed a large population exchange between Greece and Turkey.

title: The Great Kanto earthquake devastates Tokyo and Yokohama
summary: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake struck the Kanto plain at midday, and fires destroyed much of Tokyo and Yokohama, killing over 100,000 people.
reason: The quake came from a rupture along the plate boundary under Sagami Bay, and lunchtime cooking fires spread among wooden houses.
significance: It was one of the deadliest earthquakes in history and was followed by massacres of Koreans in Japan.

title: The Republic of Turkey is proclaimed
summary: The Grand National Assembly proclaimed Turkey a republic and elected Mustafa Kemal as its first president.
reason: With the sultanate abolished and peace secured at Lausanne, Kemal wanted a modern secular state.
significance: It founded the modern Turkish state and launched sweeping reforms.

title: Hitler stages the Beer Hall Putsch in Munich
summary: Adolf Hitler and the Nazi party tried to seize power in Munich, starting at the Burgerbraukeller beer hall; the coup collapsed the next day when police opened fire.
reason: Hyperinflation and the occupation of the Ruhr had shaken the Weimar Republic, and Hitler hoped to copy Mussolini's march on Rome.
significance: Hitler's trial and imprisonment gave him national fame and the time to write Mein Kampf.

title: Vladimir Lenin dies
summary: Vladimir Lenin, founder of the Soviet state, died at his estate in Gorki near Moscow after a series of strokes.
reason: Lenin's health had failed since 1922, partly linked to an assassination attempt in 1918.
significance: His death opened a power struggle that Joseph Stalin won.
wikipedia: Death and state funeral of Vladimir Lenin

title: Turkey abolishes the Ottoman Caliphate
summary: The Turkish Grand National Assembly abolished the caliphate and expelled the last caliph, Abdulmejid II, and the Ottoman family from the country.
reason: Mustafa Kemal saw the caliphate as a rival center of power and an obstacle to a secular republic.
significance: It ended an institution that had led Sunni Islam for centuries.

title: John Logie Baird demonstrates television
summary: John Logie Baird gave the first public demonstration of television transmitting moving images to members of the Royal Institution in his London laboratory.
reason: Baird had worked for years on a mechanical scanning system to send live images electrically.
significance: It marked the beginning of television, which became the dominant medium of the century.
place: 22 Frith Street, Soho, London, United Kingdom

title: Robert Goddard launches the first liquid-fueled rocket
summary: Robert Goddard launched a small rocket fueled by gasoline and liquid oxygen from a farm in Auburn, Massachusetts; it flew for about two and a half seconds.
reason: Goddard believed liquid propellants could power rockets to high altitudes and eventually into space.
significance: It founded modern rocketry, which led to spaceflight and missiles.

title: Chiang Kai-shek launches the Northern Expedition
summary: The National Revolutionary Army under Chiang Kai-shek set out from Guangzhou on a military campaign to defeat the warlords and unify China.
reason: The Kuomintang, allied with the Communists and Soviet advisers, aimed to end warlord rule over most of China.
significance: It brought China under nominal Nationalist rule by 1928 and ended the Beiyang government.

title: Chiang Kai-shek purges the Communists in Shanghai
summary: Nationalist troops and gangsters loyal to Chiang Kai-shek attacked Communists and labor unions in Shanghai, killing hundreds and arresting many more.
reason: Chiang feared growing Communist power within the Nationalist movement and was backed by Shanghai business interests.
significance: It ended the First United Front and began the long Chinese Civil War.

title: Lindbergh takes off on the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight
summary: Charles Lindbergh took off from Roosevelt Field, New York, in the Spirit of St. Louis and landed in Paris about 33 hours later, the first solo nonstop flight across the Atlantic.
reason: Lindbergh was competing for the Orteig Prize for the first nonstop flight between New York and Paris.
significance: It made Lindbergh a world celebrity and sparked a boom in public interest in aviation.
place: Roosevelt Field, Long Island, United States

title: Communists rise in the Nanchang Uprising
summary: Communist-led troops under Zhou Enlai, He Long and Zhu De seized the city of Nanchang before being driven out by Nationalist forces days later.
reason: After the Nationalists' purge, the Communists decided to launch armed resistance.
significance: It is regarded as the founding of the People's Liberation Army, whose anniversary is 1 August.

title: The Jazz Singer premieres with synchronized speech
summary: Warner Bros. premiered The Jazz Singer, starring Al Jolson, in New York, the first feature film with synchronized dialogue and singing.
reason: Warner Bros. gambled on the Vitaphone sound-on-disc system to compete with larger studios.
significance: It started the talkie era and quickly ended silent cinema.
place: Warner Theatre, New York City, United States

title: Alexander Fleming discovers penicillin
summary: At St Mary's Hospital in London, Alexander Fleming noticed that a mold contaminating a culture plate had killed the surrounding Staphylococcus bacteria.
reason: Fleming was studying bacteria and, returning from holiday, examined plates left out during his absence.
significance: Penicillin, developed into a drug in the 1940s, began the age of antibiotics and saved countless lives.
place: St Mary's Hospital, Paddington, London, United Kingdom

title: Black Tuesday: the Wall Street Crash
summary: Panic selling on the New York Stock Exchange drove prices to collapse, completing the crash that had started days earlier and wiping out billions of dollars.
reason: Speculation, buying on margin and an overvalued market left investors exposed when confidence broke.
significance: The crash helped trigger the Great Depression, which spread around the world.
place: New York Stock Exchange, New York City, United States

title: Indian nationalists declare Purna Swaraj
summary: The Indian National Congress publicly celebrated its declaration of Purna Swaraj, complete independence from British rule, with oaths taken across India.
reason: Britain had failed to grant dominion status, and Congress under Jawaharlal Nehru adopted full independence as its goal.
significance: India later chose 26 January as Republic Day when its constitution took effect in 1950.

title: Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto
summary: Clyde Tombaugh at Lowell Observatory in Flagstaff, Arizona, identified a moving object on photographic plates, which became known as Pluto.
reason: Lowell Observatory was continuing Percival Lowell's search for a Planet X beyond Neptune.
significance: Pluto was counted as the ninth planet until it was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

title: Gandhi begins the Salt March
summary: Mohandas Gandhi set out from Sabarmati Ashram with 78 followers on a 24-day walk to Dandi on the coast to make salt in defiance of the British salt tax.
reason: The salt tax was a symbol of British rule that hurt every Indian, making it an ideal target for civil disobedience.
significance: It drew world attention to the Indian independence movement and launched a mass civil disobedience campaign.

title: The first FIFA World Cup kicks off in Uruguay
summary: The first FIFA World Cup began with matches in Montevideo; France beat Mexico in the opening game, and Uruguay went on to win the tournament.
reason: FIFA wanted a world championship for football separate from the Olympics, and Uruguay, the Olympic champion, offered to host it.
significance: The World Cup became the most watched sporting event on Earth.

title: The Second Spanish Republic is proclaimed
summary: After republicans swept municipal elections, a republic was proclaimed in Madrid and King Alfonso XIII left Spain.
reason: The monarchy was discredited by its support of Miguel Primo de Rivera's dictatorship.
significance: The republic's deep divisions led to the Spanish Civil War five years later.

title: The Mukden Incident gives Japan a pretext to seize Manchuria
summary: Japanese officers blew up a section of railway near Mukden, blamed Chinese soldiers, and used it as a pretext for the Kwantung Army to invade Manchuria.
reason: Japanese militarists wanted Manchuria's resources and territory and acted without approval from Tokyo.
significance: It led to the puppet state of Manchukuo and exposed the League of Nations' weakness.

title: The Statute of Westminster grants dominions full independence
summary: The British Parliament passed the Statute of Westminster, giving the dominions such as Canada, Australia, New Zealand and South Africa legislative independence.
reason: The dominions had grown into nations and demanded legal equality with Britain, as recognized in the Balfour Declaration of 1926.
significance: It turned the British Empire into the Commonwealth of equal nations.

title: Japan sets up the puppet state of Manchukuo
summary: Japan proclaimed the state of Manchukuo in Manchuria, installing the former Qing emperor Puyi as its head with its capital at Changchun.
reason: After conquering Manchuria, Japan wanted a nominally independent regime to control the region's resources.
significance: It deepened conflict with China and led Japan to leave the League of Nations.

title: Siam's absolute monarchy is overthrown
summary: The Khana Ratsadon, a group of civilians and officers, staged a bloodless coup in Bangkok and forced King Prajadhipok to accept a constitution.
reason: Western-educated reformers resented royal privilege, and the Great Depression had strained the economy.
significance: It ended absolute monarchy in Siam, now Thailand.

title: Ibn Saud proclaims the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
summary: Abdulaziz Ibn Saud united his domains of the Hejaz and Nejd into a single kingdom named Saudi Arabia.
reason: After decades of conquest across the Arabian peninsula, Ibn Saud sought to consolidate his realm under one name and crown.
significance: It founded the Saudi state, which became a central power in the Middle East and the oil economy.

title: Adolf Hitler is appointed Chancellor of Germany
summary: President Paul von Hindenburg appointed Nazi party leader Adolf Hitler as Chancellor at the head of a coalition government.
reason: The Depression had fueled Nazi support, and conservative elites believed they could control Hitler.
significance: It began the Nazi dictatorship that led to World War II and the Holocaust.

title: The Reichstag building burns
summary: The German parliament building in Berlin was set on fire; a Dutch communist, Marinus van der Lubbe, was arrested at the scene.
reason: The Nazis blamed a communist plot and used the fire as a pretext for emergency measures.
significance: The Reichstag Fire Decree suspended civil liberties and paved the way for dictatorship.

title: Franklin D. Roosevelt takes office and launches the New Deal
summary: Franklin D. Roosevelt was inaugurated as US president, declaring that the only thing to fear was fear itself, and began a burst of emergency economic legislation.
reason: The Great Depression had left a quarter of workers jobless and the banking system near collapse.
significance: The New Deal reshaped the role of the US federal government in the economy.
place: United States Capitol, Washington, D.C., United States
wikipedia: First inauguration of Franklin D. Roosevelt

title: The Reichstag passes the Enabling Act
summary: Meeting in the Kroll Opera House, the Reichstag passed a law allowing Hitler's cabinet to make laws without parliament, with only the Social Democrats voting against.
reason: Hitler sought legal cover for dictatorship, using intimidation and promises to win the needed two-thirds majority.
significance: It gave Hitler dictatorial power and ended Weimar democracy.

title: Hitler purges rivals in the Night of the Long Knives
summary: Hitler had SA leader Ernst Rohm and dozens of other rivals arrested and murdered by the SS over several days, starting at Bad Wiessee.
reason: Hitler wanted to remove the SA as a threat and win the loyalty of the army.
significance: It consolidated Hitler's absolute power and established the SS as the regime's terror arm.

title: The Chinese Red Army begins the Long March
summary: Encircled by Nationalist forces, about 86,000 troops of the Red Army broke out of the Jiangxi Soviet and began a retreat of thousands of kilometers.
reason: Chiang Kai-shek's encirclement campaigns had made the Communist base in Jiangxi untenable.
significance: It saved the Chinese Communist Party and brought Mao Zedong to its leadership.

title: Nazi Germany enacts the Nuremberg Laws
summary: At the Nazi party rally in Nuremberg, the Reichstag passed laws stripping Jews of German citizenship and banning marriage between Jews and non-Jews.
reason: The Nazi regime's racial ideology aimed to exclude Jews from German society.
significance: It gave legal form to Nazi antisemitism and was a step toward the Holocaust.

title: Italy invades Ethiopia
summary: Italian troops crossed from Eritrea into Ethiopia without a declaration of war, beginning the Second Italo-Ethiopian War.
reason: Mussolini sought an empire and revenge for Italy's defeat at Adwa in 1896.
significance: The League of Nations' failure to stop the invasion discredited collective security.

title: German troops reoccupy the Rhineland
summary: German troops marched into the demilitarized Rhineland in breach of the Treaty of Versailles and the Locarno Treaties; France and Britain did not respond with force.
reason: Hitler gambled that the Western powers, divided and war-weary, would not act.
significance: Its success encouraged Hitler's later aggression and weakened France's security.

title: Military uprising starts the Spanish Civil War
summary: Army officers rose against the Spanish Republic, starting in Melilla in Spanish Morocco; the coup's partial failure led to a three-year civil war.
reason: Right-wing officers opposed the Popular Front government and feared revolution.
significance: The war ended in Franco's dictatorship and was a prelude to World War II.

title: The Berlin Olympics open
summary: Hitler opened the Summer Olympics in Berlin, where Jesse Owens won four gold medals in athletics.
reason: Nazi Germany used the Games to showcase the regime and its claims of racial superiority.
significance: The Games became a symbol of sport used as propaganda, and Owens's victories its rebuttal.

title: Chiang Kai-shek is detained in the Xi'an Incident
summary: Generals Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng detained Chiang Kai-shek at Xi'an and forced him to agree to stop fighting the Communists and resist Japan.
reason: Many Chinese officers believed the war against the Communists should give way to defense against Japanese aggression.
significance: It led to the Second United Front against Japan and saved the Communists from defeat.

title: German and Italian bombers destroy Guernica
summary: Aircraft of the German Condor Legion and the Italian air force bombed the Basque town of Guernica on market day, killing hundreds of civilians.
reason: Franco's Nationalists and their allies sought to break Basque resistance and test aerial bombing tactics.
significance: It became a symbol of the horror of war against civilians, immortalized by Picasso's painting.

title: The Hindenburg airship bursts into flames
summary: The German passenger airship Hindenburg caught fire while docking at Lakehurst, New Jersey, killing 36 people in front of newsreel cameras.
reason: The airship was filled with flammable hydrogen, and a spark is thought to have ignited leaking gas.
significance: The disaster ended the era of passenger airships.
place: Naval Air Station Lakehurst, New Jersey, United States

title: Marco Polo Bridge Incident starts the Second Sino-Japanese War
summary: A clash between Japanese and Chinese troops near the Marco Polo Bridge outside Beijing escalated into full-scale war between Japan and China.
reason: Japan had been expanding into northern China, and both sides refused to back down after the skirmish.
significance: It began the Second Sino-Japanese War, which merged into World War II and killed millions.

title: Japanese troops capture Nanjing and begin the Nanjing Massacre
summary: Japanese forces took China's capital Nanjing and over the following weeks killed tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of civilians and prisoners and committed mass rapes.
reason: Japanese commanders tolerated and encouraged brutality after fierce fighting at Shanghai.
significance: It remains one of the worst atrocities of the twentieth century and a deep wound in Chinese-Japanese relations.

title: Oil is struck in commercial quantity in Saudi Arabia
summary: American geologists of the California Arabian Standard Oil Company struck oil in commercial quantities at the Dammam No. 7 well near Dhahran.
reason: After years of dry wells, the company kept drilling deeper on the advice of geologist Max Steineke.
significance: It turned Saudi Arabia into one of the world's leading oil producers.

title: Germany annexes Austria in the Anschluss
summary: German troops crossed into Austria unopposed, and Hitler announced its union with Germany the next day.
reason: Hitler wanted to unite all Germans in one Reich, and he moved to stop Chancellor Schuschnigg's referendum on independence.
significance: It was Hitler's first annexation of a sovereign state and showed the Western powers would not resist.

title: Mexico nationalizes its oil industry
summary: President Lazaro Cardenas announced the expropriation of the assets of foreign oil companies in Mexico, leading to the creation of Pemex.
reason: The foreign companies refused to obey a Supreme Court ruling to raise workers' wages and improve conditions.
significance: It became a symbol of Mexican sovereignty and an early model for resource nationalism.

title: Chinese forces breach the Yellow River dikes
summary: Nationalist troops broke the Yellow River dikes at Huayuankou to slow the Japanese advance, flooding vast areas of Henan, Anhui and Jiangsu.
reason: Chiang Kai-shek's government sought to halt Japanese forces heading toward Wuhan.
significance: The flood killed hundreds of thousands of civilians and left millions homeless, one of the deadliest acts of environmental warfare.

title: The Munich Agreement hands the Sudetenland to Germany
summary: Germany, Britain, France and Italy signed an agreement in Munich allowing Germany to annex the Sudetenland of Czechoslovakia, which was not consulted.
reason: Britain and France, unready for war, hoped to satisfy Hitler through appeasement.
significance: It became the classic example of failed appeasement on the road to World War II.

title: Kristallnacht pogrom across Nazi Germany
summary: Nazi paramilitaries and civilians attacked Jewish homes, shops and synagogues across Germany and Austria, killing dozens and sending about 30,000 Jewish men to concentration camps.
reason: The regime used the killing of a German diplomat in Paris by a young Polish Jew as a pretext for organized violence.
significance: It marked a shift from discrimination to open violence against Jews, foreshadowing the Holocaust.

title: Hahn and Strassmann discover nuclear fission
summary: In Berlin, Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann detected barium after bombarding uranium with neutrons, which Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch soon explained as the splitting of the nucleus.
reason: Physicists across Europe were studying what happened when uranium was bombarded with neutrons.
significance: It opened the way to nuclear power and the atomic bomb.
place: Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Chemistry, Berlin, Germany

title: A living coelacanth is identified in South Africa
summary: Museum curator Marjorie Courtenay-Latimer found a strange fish in a trawler's catch at East London, which J. L. B. Smith identified as a coelacanth, thought extinct for 66 million years.
reason: Courtenay-Latimer asked local fishermen to send her unusual specimens for the town museum.
significance: It was one of the great zoological finds of the century, a living fossil linking fish and land vertebrates.
